title: VLA and ALMA observations of the lensed radio-quiet quasar SDSS J0924+0219: a molecular structure in a 3 μJy radio source
question: What are the properties of the radio and molecular gas reservoirs in the lensed radio-quiet quasar SDSS J0924+0219, and what causes its optical flux ratio anomaly?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image VLA and ALMA observations and generate moment maps
recipe.method: Run VLA and ALMA CASA calibration pipelines, image with CLEAN using natural and Briggs (robust = 0.0) weighting, convolve VLA map to ALMA beam, and compute moment 1 and 2 maps with a 4-sigma pixel threshold.
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.0; SNR > 4 pixel cut for moment maps

recipe.goal: Fit four elliptical Gaussian components to lensed images in the image plane
recipe.method: Fit four elliptical Gaussians at the image positions in the CO(5-4) and radio maps using a 10-parameter optimization, and test point-source Gaussian fits with AIPS JMFIT.
key_parameters: 10 parameters: 4 peak flux densities, FWHMs and axis ratios of A (=D) and B (=C), 2 positional offsets (x, y); major axes fixed tangential to lens centre (100.87, 77.21, 12.99, 151.07 deg)
assumptions: FWHMs and axis ratios of A and D are equal, and those of B and C are equal; FWHMs constrained to be greater than major axis of dirty beam

recipe.goal: Model gravitational lensing in the image plane
recipe.method: Optimize a Gaussian source profile and flux anomaly parameter f_AD through an SIE lens galaxy mass model against the CO(5-4), submm continuum, and radio images.
software: lens modelling code developed by Neal Jackson
key_parameters: SIE lens parameters: critical radius 0.87 arcsec, ellipticity 0.13 at PA -73.1 deg, shear 0.042 at PA 65.4 deg; f_AD between 0 and 1
assumptions: Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid (SIE) lens mass profile and Gaussian source profile

recipe.goal: Fit four elliptical Gaussian components directly to u-v visibilities
recipe.method: Fit four elliptical Gaussians to the continuum-subtracted CO(5-4) and radio visibility data using uvmultifit with image positions fixed to Inada et al. (2003).
key_parameters: Image positions and position angles fixed; 8 free parameters for CO (4 fluxes, 2 widths, 2 axis ratios); 6 free parameters for radio (4 fluxes, 1 width, 1 axis ratio)
assumptions: Optical image positions from Inada et al. (2003) apply to CO and radio components

recipe.goal: Perform lens modelling in the u-v plane and derive intrinsic CO luminosity and dynamical mass
recipe.method: Fit a Sersic source profile lensed by an SIE galaxy model to the CO(5-4), submm continuum, and radio visibilities using visilens, then compute intrinsic CO luminosity and dynamical mass following Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005).
key_parameters: Einstein radius = 0.92 arcsec (optimized on CO visibilities, fixed for continuum and radio); Sersic source profile
assumptions: Disk radius R is half the FWHM of the integrated CO source (81 mas); flat cosmology with DL = 11400 Mpc, DA = 1790 Mpc

recipe.goal: Reconstruct velocity-resolved CO(5-4) source structure across frequency channels
recipe.method: Project each frequency slice of the ALMA CO(5-4) image cube back to the source plane using the fixed SIE lens model, modelling the source in each channel as a single elliptical Gaussian.
software: lens modelling code developed by Neal Jackson
key_parameters: 5 free source parameters per frequency slice: position (x, y), flux, width, axis ratio, position angle
assumptions: Single elliptical Gaussian source per frequency channel acts as regularisation

recipe.goal: Fit FIR-to-radio spectral energy distribution (SED) and compute q_IR
recipe.method: Combine ALMA submm continuum and VLA radio flux densities with literature data to calculate q_IR and fit a modified blackbody curve to the SED.
key_parameters: Dust temperature T and emissivity index beta
assumptions: Optically thin modified blackbody S_nu proportional to nu^(3+beta) / (exp(h*nu/kT) - 1)

recipe.goal: Simulate microlensing magnification map for image D
recipe.method: Generate a microlensing magnification map for image D using Wambsganss (2001) ray-tracing tree code and convolve with a Gaussian optical source profile to evaluate demagnification duration.
software: ray-tracing tree code developed by Wambsganss (2001)
key_parameters: Map side-length 100 eta_0, resolution 0.005 eta_0/pixel, (kappa, gamma) = (0.48, 0.57), stellar surface density fraction alpha = 0.07, eta_0 ~ 3.2e16 cm, <M/M_sun> = 0.3, v_trans = 0.049 eta_0/year, R_1/2 = 0.02 eta_0 and 0.06 eta_0
assumptions: Standard accretion disc model size R_1/2 = 0.02 eta_0 (also tested 3x larger, R_1/2 = 0.06 eta_0)
